The Data Recipient agrees to process the Data only for the following purposes agreed with the HSCIC: 
Objective for processing:
5.1       AQuA Organisational Context
Advancing Quality Alliance (AQuA) was established in 2010 by the Strategic Health Authority, as a: not for profit; membership body; which is part of Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust (SRFT).  Advancing Quality Alliance is funded by our 72 member organisations that include: Foundation Trusts, Mental Health Trusts, and Clinical Commissioning Groups.  AQuA’s core membership is based in North West England (covering a population of c. 7.5 million) with some cross-border members from Yorkshire (covering a population of 0.75 million). Membership from other health or social care organisations would be considered.  Members pay an annual fee and draw down services as appropriate to their local improvement needs.  All of the membership income is used to invest in member organisation health improvement. 

AQUA provide services in a number of ways :-
-           Through a membership arrangement with individual NHS and Social Care organisations (who pay a fee for access to AQuA’s service and regionally based expertise).  
-           on an ad-hoc basis (per service offered) to NHS and Social Care organisations
-           In respect of income received from grant bodies (bid to be awarded via charity, nonprofit making, covering costs only).
All of the above carry charges which are charged on a cost recovery basis. 
AHSNs may also commission work to support their health objectives.  If tendered, AQuA may bid for aspects of this work which align to our organisation business objectives.    AQuA would be bidding on a not for profit basis.  Additionally, AQUA confirms that they will not use ONS data for tendering or any other commercial purpose.

Our vision is ‘to support AQuA’s members and customers to transform the health and quality of healthcare of people they serve’. 

AQuA’s hosting arrangements with SRFT are to provide the statutory accountability for AQuA to operate as an NHS organisation; AQuA does not have independent legal status. The relationship is therefore to provide governance and service infrastructure.  AQuA is not therefore a commercial arm of SRFT.

5.2       Data 
The data is requested solely to enable the delivery of services by AQUA as outlined below, and will not be used for any other purpose.  
Within this application “NHS and Social Care” is used as shorthand to include NHS or Social Care providers, commissioners, Local Authorities (in relation to delivering their public health duties only), CSUs, GP Practices and national NHS and Social Care organisations.  It also includes private sector providers of health, in relation to the services provided by those private sector healthcare providers under NHS or Social Care contract.

AQuA requires the data to be held for multiple years to provide longitudinal analysis to identify trends and year on year comparison.  The nature of the data analysis will change over the life of the data extract based on the specific area being reviewed i.e. the latest healthcare issue e.g. readmissions, mortality, Sepsis etc. 

The services broadly fall in to two categories – a programme of work for a particular year which is established as part of AQUA’s strategic plan which is agreed with its members; and a grant or development programme which may generate the following year’s programme of work.  Quality improvement programmes may be developed based on AQuA research to establish ‘what the data says’. 

5.2.1    To support AQuA Programmes
5.2.1.1 Mortality
In-depth Mortality Reviews
Objectives 
AQUA work with provider trusts [and their partners] to provide a ‘whole-system’ review of their Governance, Systems, Processes and Information Management. As part of this review, AQUA undertake detailed analysis of HES data to ascertain if the trust is an outlier in any of the scores of ‘indicators’ that AQUA examine. AQUA also undertake themed analysis [e.g. “Patient Flow”] to see if there is any pattern in potential challenges of a similar nature across several aspects of care [e.g. A&E wait times, times of admission, episodes per spell, bed occupancy rates, delayed discharge].
The mortality reviews assess a multitude of data fields from publically held data as well as local data sources. This is triangulated and explored further with organisational/ economy
wide interviews and focus groups. 
The data used within this service is both HES and ONS data.
The service may be accessed by member organisations, but also by non-member NHS and Social Care organisations.

Reducing Mortality Collaboratives and Regional Work
Objectives
A mortality collaborative network, looking at how best to tackle the challenges associated
with high hospital Mortality Rates. It is based on the original five key drivers of clinical care, reliable care, documentation and Information, leadership and end of life care. Working with up to 10 teams on focussed activity, which may be speciality or challenge-based themes. These are likely to include topical areas of interest such as sepsis, acute kidney injury, pneumonia and the care of the deteriorating patient. Action learning sets will provide a platform for wider organisation involvement across the membership and beyond. Advancing Quality Alliance aim to have a series of masterclass opportunities and at year end a further lessons learnt publication will be developed.

5.2.1.2 Advancing Quality [AQ]
Objectives
The Advancing Quality (AQ) programme is AQuA’s flagship offering having a significant impact in terms of improving the quality of care and reducing avoidable mortality.  The AQ programme is funded by north-west CCGs and all northwest acute trusts and specialist mental health providers participate in the programme.  

It is operated in twelve hospital conditions and two in mental health. These include metrics along whole pathways in areas such as diabetes and asthma.
Advancing Quality:
•           Focuses on issues that matter locally, underpinned by robust provider and commissioner involvement
•           Adopts and spreads best practice
•           Creates high quality, benchmarked information to help local systems understand their current performance and health inequalities, and to inform the development of improvement strategies whilst tackling unwarranted variation
•           Uses information to develop shared priorities based on outcomes that are in greatest need of improvement and comparing that information with peers to drive up further improvements

5.2.1.3 Improving Outcome Packs
Objectives
AQuA’s Improving Outcomes Packs are a ‘one stop’ resource to save you time; they provide benchmarking data and analysis to help identify where to focus your improvement efforts and access to resources to help you. AQuA has produced six packs to date covering Stroke, Chronic Kidney Disease, Chronic Liver disease, COPD, Asthma and Diabetes.

AQUA produce a series of condition-specific information packs that provide a host of benchmarked data across a wide range of data-sets including HES (no data sources have identifiable data, all others are aggregated data, and/or indicators, none are at patient level). The aim is to support CCGs, working with local partner organisations, to improve the care of patients in their area.

This service is provided to members only, and does not attract a separate charge.

5.2.1.4             Enhanced Recovery Programme
Objectives
Enhanced Recovery is an example of pathway redesign that focuses on the quality and experience of care and actively involves patients and families within local quality improvement work.
5.2.1.6 Patient Safety
Objectives
Advancing Quality Alliance have an extensive Patient Safety programme. This includes a recent successful Health Foundation bid to test the application of the Charles Vincent Framework and plans to produce a regular “Safety Report”. Testing the CV framework will inform learning and may improve safety at the two test sites and, ultimately, across the county. 
This service is provided under a specific charitable grant bid.
